prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key commitments and targets (non-ideological)

Governing approach and fiscal rules
- “Mission-driven” government with five missions: highest sustained G7 growth; clean power by 2030; halve serious violent crime; break down barriers to opportunity; build an NHS fit for the future.
- Fiscal rules: current budget to balance and debt falling as a share of GDP by year 5; strengthen the OBR; Covid Corruption Commissioner.
- No increases to National Insurance, Income Tax rates or VAT; abolish non-dom status; close avoidance loopholes; modernise HMRC.

Economy, industry and investment
- Industrial Strategy and statutory Industrial Strategy Council; sector plans (automotive, life sciences, creative).
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to leverage 3:1 private investment: ports (£1.8bn), gigafactories (£1.5bn), steel (£2.5bn), carbon capture (£1bn), green hydrogen (£0.5bn).
- Corporation tax capped at 25% for the Parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- Late payment crackdown; British Business Bank reform; procurement access for SMEs.

Infrastructure, transport and housing
- 10-year infrastructure strategy; National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; full gigabit and national 5G by 2030.
- Roads: fix 1m potholes/year; support EV transition (restore 2030 ICE phase-out, more charge points, battery info standard).
- Rail: bring passenger services into public ownership as contracts expire; Great British Railways; more bus franchising powers and lift ban on municipal ownership.
- Build 1.5m homes over the Parliament; restore mandatory targets; fund planning officers via higher non-UK buyer surcharge; brownfield first plus strategic “grey belt” release; new towns; strengthen affordable/social housing; permanent mortgage guarantee; first-time buyer first-refusal.

Work, immigration and skills
- New Deal for Working People: ban exploitative zero-hours and “fire and rehire”; day-one rights (parental leave, sick pay, unfair dismissal); Single Enforcement Body; minimum wage remit to reflect cost of living; remove age bands.
- Reform points-based immigration; reduce net migration; stronger enforcement; link migration to domestic skills plans; bolster MAC.
- Employment support: merge Jobcentre Plus and National Careers Service; youth guarantee (18–21): training/apprenticeship/work support; two weeks’ work experience for every pupil.

Energy, climate, nature and water
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; advance nuclear (Hinkley, Sizewell C, SMRs); maintain gas reserve.
- No new North Sea exploration licences; no new coal; ban fracking; tighten windfall tax (extend, +3pp, remove allowances).
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn), HQ in Scotland; Local Power Plan; British Jobs Bonus (£500m/yr).
- Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn) to upgrade 5m homes; PRS minimum efficiency by 2030.
- Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism; restore BoE climate mandate; require credible corporate transition plans.
- Nature: National River Walks (9), 3 new National Forests; expand habitats. Water: special measures for water firms, tougher fines, bonus blocks, criminal charges, independent outlet monitoring.
- Farming: 50% of public sector food local or higher standard; land-use framework; end badger cull; stronger animal welfare (ban trail hunting, trophy imports, puppy smuggling/farming, snares; phase down animal testing).

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee (thousands of officers/PCSOs/specials); efficiency programme to fund.
- New Respect Orders; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers; knife crime plan (mandatory YOT referral; curfews/tagging; ban zombie/ninja blades; online sales controls with executive liability); Young Futures hubs nationwide.
- VAWG: specialist rape units in every force; fast-track rape cases with specialist courts; DA experts in 999; legal advocates in each force area; spiking offence; stronger stalking tools.
- Police standards: mandatory vetting/misconduct rules; HMICFRS intervention powers; safeguards on child strip-searching.
- Courts: use Associate Prosecutors; strengthen Victims’ Commissioner; sentencing review. Prisons: build capacity; reduce reoffending via education/jobs/housing; probation governance review. Historical injustices: Hillsborough Law; Windrush Commissioner; act on Infected Blood/Grenfell/Covid inquiries.

Education and families
- 6,500 new teachers; restore support staff negotiating body; leadership and regional improvement programmes; Ofsted single grade replaced by report card; MAT inspections; curriculum/assessment review; SEND inclusion.
- 3,000 school-based nurseries; review parental leave; free breakfast clubs in every primary; cap branded uniform items; mental health professionals in every school; Young Futures hubs.
- Skills England; devolve adult skills; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform Apprenticeship Levy to Growth and Skills Levy; secure HE funding and standards.
- Creative access, PE time, national museum loans, music education network; ticket resale protections; football regulator.

Health and care
- Cut NHS waits: 40,000 extra weekly appointments (c.2m/yr); shared waiting lists; use independent sector; publish workforce plans.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; NHS innovation/adoption strategy; expand clinical trials; enhanced NHS app.
- Maternity safety focus; more midwives; digitise Red Book; regulate managers; Royal College of Clinical Leadership; implement Cass Review recommendations.
- Primary care: more GPs; face-to-face on request; continuity; pharmacist prescribing; wider direct/self-referrals; pilot Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry: 700k urgent appointments; recruit to shortage areas; contract reform; supervised toothbrushing (ages 3–5).
- National Care Service with national standards; “home first”; Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care; guaranteed family visits.
- Mental health: 8,500 extra staff; modernise Mental Health Act; reduce suicide; address detention disparities.
- Public health: smoke-free generation; restrict youth-targeted vape branding; ban junk food ads to children and energy drink sales to under-16s; strengthen online safety; gambling reforms. Target: halve gap in healthy life expectancy between regions; end new HIV cases by 2030.

Standards and constitutional reform
- Independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; empower Ministerial Adviser; ban MPs’ paid advisory/consultancy roles; Commons modernisation.
- Lords: end hereditary peers; mandatory retirement at 80; participation standards; longer-term replacement with a more representative second chamber (consultation).
- Improve voter registration; fix ID anomalies; votes at 16; tighter donation rules.

Devolution and foreign policy
- Strengthen intergovernmental working; Council of the Nations and Regions; devolve employment support (Wales) and explore justice devolution.
- Defence: Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% GDP; NATO and nuclear deterrent; defence industrial strategy; Armed Forces Commissioner; scrap visa fees for non‑UK veterans (4+ years).
- Ukraine support; AUKUS; China strategy audit; support for Hong Kong BN(O) arrivals; protect Overseas Territories.
- Trade: publish trade strategy; targeted FTAs and sector deals; WTO/CPTPP engagement; OECD minimum tax; pursue India FTA; deepen Gulf/Africa partnerships.
- Middle East: immediate ceasefire, hostages released, humanitarian aid; recognise Palestinian state as part of a process to a two‑state solution.
- Development: rebuild capability; priority themes (economy, debt, women/girls, conflict prevention, climate finance); restore 0.7% ODA when fiscal conditions allow.
